package: W54-01 — provable checkpoint GC and durable write ordering
question: Can crashed or abandoned checkpoint objects and intents be reclaimed without risking a live capture or a referenced rollback object?
answer: Yes, under the store lock after transaction recovery, and only when the full reference set validates; every uncertain case retains the affected set.

behavior.objects: delete 64-hex regular files no valid manifest references; caps 2,000 manifests and 100,000 objects
behavior.intents: delete only when pid is dead and manifestDigest is undefined
behavior.retained: unknown object names, symlinks, invalid/unreadable manifests, live pids, over-cap stores
behavior.order: intent -> objects -> manifest -> effects; each durable writer fsyncs the file, renames, fsyncs the directory

added: recovery sweeps unreferenced objects and intents whose creator died before capture

residuals: Hardware-level power loss (device caches, torn writes) is not measurable in this environment; the claim is limited to the recorded fsync order.
Unreferenced manifests are retained, so a manifest with no session association keeps its objects by design.
Store directories beyond the scan caps are left untouched until a later recovery has room.
